full_judgment:
Md Zakir Hossain, J: At the instance of the defendant-respondent-petitioner, the Rule was issued to examine the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree dated 1-9-2013 (decree being drawn on 9-9-2013) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Lalmonirhat in Family Appeal No.5 of 2011 affirming the judgment and decree dated 7-4-2011 (decree being drawn on 12-4-2011) passed by the learned Assistant Judge and Family Court, Sadar, Lalmonirhat decreeing the Family Suit No. 42 of 2008. 

 5. After conclusion of the trial, the learned Judge, Family Court, was pleased to decree the suit in part in believing the 2nd kabinnama was not legal. 

 7. Mr Sonjoy Kurmar Kunda, the learned Advocate of the petitioner submits that the learned Assistant Judge of the Family Court without considering the evidence on record from true perspective most illegally decreed the suit and the Appellate Court without considering the facts and circumstances of the specific allegations set out in the pleadings of the defendant concurred with the finding of the Trial Court so far it relates to the 2nd kabinnama and dower money. Therefore, the judgment and decree of the Courts below suffer from misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of 1st kabinnama from legal perspective. Consequently, the judgment and decree of the Courts below are liable to be turned down to secure the ends of justice. He further submits that the plaintiff-petitioner admitted that :he marriage was solemnized on 17-6-2005 and stoutly denied the execution of 2nd kabinnama which was created by practicing false personification and, as such, decreed as to dower money to the tune of Taka 15,00,000 instead of Taka 2,01,001. 

 8. Mr Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan along with Shahanara Begum, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party submits that the learned Judge of the Family Court after considering the evidence on record from their correct perspective and legal position involved in this case was pleased to decree the suit and the Appellate Court after its independent and dispassionate consideration of evidence on record was pleased to concur with the finding as to the 2nd kabinnama and quantum of the dower money. Therefore, there is no reason to interfere with the same. He further submits that there is no legal bar in enhancing the dower money by the 2nd or subsequent kabinnama. Therefore, the 2nd or subsequent kabinnama is not illegal. He further submits that the signature of the defendant as mentioned in exhibit-1 dated 17-6-2005 that is his 1st kabinnama and the disputed signature as mentioned in the 2nd kabinnama appears to be similar and unison. Therefore, there is no apparent reason to disprove the 2nd kabinnama and, as such, the Rule is liable to be knocked down by this Court to secure the ends of justice. He further submits that Muslim Marriage is a contract and dower is a condition of the contract and contract may be renewed subsequently. Therefore, the petitioner is bound to discharge his obligation by paying dower money as mentioned in the 2nd kabinnama. He further submits that the amount of dower may be fixed either before or at the time of marriage or after marriage and it can be increased after marriage. He further submits that the liability of husband to pay the dower and maintenance to his wife on dissolution of marriage cannot be denied as the wife is legally entitled to dower money as well as maintenance. 

 10. Taking thread from the judgment of the Nasir Ahmed Khan vs Mst. Ismat Jahan Begum 21 DLR (SC) 145, he submits that without being undue influence or intimidation, the defendant petitioner voluntarily executed the 2nd kabinnama; therefore, he is bound by terms and conditions stipulated in the 2nd kabinnama. He further submits that when the marriage is admittedly dissolved by at the instance of the husband, the wife is legally entitled to dower money as stipulated in the kabinnama. He further submits that the petitioner in order to deprive the plaintiff to enjoy the fruits of long cherished decree filed the instant revisional application; therefore, the same is liable to be struck down by this Court to secure the ends of justice. 

 14. Now, the pertinent question is whether the second kabinnama is genuine or not. Admittedly, the marriage of the plaintiff No. 1 and defendant was solemnized as per Muslim Shariya on 17-6-2005 fixing Taka 2,01,001 as dower money and Taka 6,000 was paid at the time of marriage which finds support from the Exhibit-1 (KA). The second kabinnama was registered on 27-10-2006 fixing Taka 15,00,000 as dower money. The execution of second kabinnama has been stoutly denied by the defendant. The Family Court disbelieves the second kabinnama. The Appellate Court believed that the second kabinnama is genuine though the plaintiff did not prefer any cross objection or appeal against the judgment and decree of the Family Court with the following observation: 

 21. But the learned Appellate Court without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and reversing the finding of the Family Court that the second kabinnama was not duly executed by the defendant most illegally held that the second kabinnama is genuine and abruptly directed the defendant to pay Taka 5,00,000 as dower money without noticing the fact of dissolution of marriage. It is true that the mode of payment of dower money has not been depicted in the kabinnama itself. Since the second kabinnama has not been proved as legal, therefore, the outstanding amount of dower money is entitled by the plaintiff No.1 and, as such, the Family Court rightly decreed that the petitioner is entitled to Taka 1,94,001 at a time. The plaintiff No.1 is entitled to Taka 1,00,000 as maintenance and the plaintiff No. 2 minor son will get Taka 2,000 per month as maintenance since 25-10-2007 till attaining his majority. 

 vii. The judgment and decree of the Appellate Court is hereby set-aside and those of the trial Court be restored.
